minutes.headline: Town Meeting rejected cutting the proposed assistant town manager/HR post from the budget, 67 to 76, after a recount.
minutes.summary: After the capital plan vote on Article 6, Town Meeting took up the Article 7 operating budget. The town manager and the new school superintendent presented, then residents debated the proposed assistant town manager/HR director and a part-time parks director. An amendment to strike the HR position's salary and insurance lines failed on a counted card vote, and the meeting moved on to DPW questions with the budget still open.

what_happened.line: Town Meeting rejected an amendment to strike the proposed assistant town manager/HR position from the Article 7 budget, after a recount of the card vote.
The moderator ordered the recount because of confusion over which sections were counted.
The town manager said the operating budget is balanced on recurring revenue, with no free cash or stabilization draw for operations.
Article 6, the capital plan, passed unanimously.
The meeting moved on to the DPW hold; the rest of the Article 7 budget continues Monday.

why_it_matters: The HR post stays in the proposed budget, which adds a permanent salaried position to the town budget, mostly taxes, in future years.
Article 7 is not yet adopted, so the remaining holds, including DPW, and the final vote on the whole budget are still ahead.
watch_next: The Monday continuation of Town Meeting, which takes up the remaining Article 7 holds, beginning with the total DPW hold.
The final vote on the Article 7 omnibus operating budget.
